_how_to_fill: Fill each entry following references/writing-descriptions.md in the bi-joe-data-profiler skill. source: system_metadata | user_documentation | inferred | pending. When source is inferred, confidence (high|medium|low) and evidence are required. The description is plain business language that says more than the name does. A column name may appear in plain text where it helps, never in backticks. grain builds on it ('One row for each ...'). Suggest BEAM annotations in beam{} following references/beam-annotations-guide.md. Then run: bijoe check <dir> and bijoe render <dir>.

dataset.summary: The policyholder, policy, claim and billing records of a Danish insurance company that sells home, car, personal, pet and travel cover to private persons. The oldest records date from 2008, while claims, payments and invoices cover January 2023 to the end of 2025.
evidence: All amounts are named DKK; street and city names are Danish (Skovvej, København K, Region Hovedstaden)
Product names: Indboforsikring, Bilforsikring, Husforsikring, Ulykkesforsikring, Rejseforsikring; ProductCategory values Bolig, Person, Bil, Dyr
Customers.SignupDate 2008-01-06 to 2025-10-31; Policies.StartDate 2008-01-06 to 2025-12-31
Claims.LossDate, ClaimPayments.PaymentDate and PremiumInvoices.InvoiceDate all start in January 2023 and end in December 2025
Customers have first name, last name, birth date and gender and no company fields, so they are private persons

Addresses.description: The Danish postal addresses, with street, house number, optional floor and postal code, that customers live at and that policies insure. An address can be shared by several customers or policies.
Addresses.grain: One row for each address, made up of a street, a house number, an optional floor and a postal code
evidence: AddressID unique, 0% missing, 2,860 rows, 50001-52860
Street 22 values, HouseNumber 1-140, ZipCode 44 distinct values, all found in PostalCodes (100%)
Floor 72.06% missing; values such as '2. tv.', '1. th.', 'st.' are Danish floor and side notations
Customers.AddressID and Policies.InsuredAddressID both point here (100% found)
open_questions: Is an address with the same street, house number, floor and postal code stored only once, or can it appear under several AddressIDs?
Addresses.ai_notes: HouseNumber + ZipCode is not unique (2,198 distinct in 2,860 rows). Only 22 distinct street names exist, so street names are reused across cities.

beam.table_why: One row per AddressID, no dates or version columns, so only current values are held.

AddressID.why: The source's own identifier for each address; unique across 2,860 rows.

Street.why: An address cannot be located without a street.

HouseNumber.why: An address cannot be located without a house number.

ZipCode.why: Every address needs a postal code; measured relationship to PostalCodes.ZipCode, 100% found.

ClaimPayments.description: A payment the company makes out of a claim to a customer or to a workshop, supplier or craftsman, tied to the cover it falls under. A claim can be paid in several instalments.
ClaimPayments.grain: One row for each payment made on a claim
evidence: PaymentID unique, 956 rows, 950001-950956
ClaimID found in Claims (100%), 658 of 850 claims have payments, up to 3 payments each
CoverageID found in Coverages (100%), 25 distinct values
PayeeType: Kunde (customer) 515, Værksted (workshop) 157, Leverandør (supplier) 146, Håndværker (craftsman) 138
AmountDKK 20-447,700; PaymentDate 2023-01-22 to 2025-12-31
open_questions: Does CoverageID show which cover of the policy paid, and is it always one of the policy's own covers?
Why do 10 combinations of claim and payment date occur twice?
ClaimPayments.ai_notes: ClaimID + CoverageID + PaymentDate is not unique (946 distinct in 956 rows), so a claim can pay the same cover twice on one day. Danish values: Kunde = customer, Værksted = workshop, Leverandør = supplier, Håndværker = craftsman.

beam.table_why: One payment date, and the row is finished when the payment is made.

PaymentID.why: The identifier for each individual payment.

PaymentDate.why: The day the payment was made.

AmountDKK.why: The amount paid out; can be summed per claim, and is central to claim cost.

Claims.description: A report from a policyholder that something insured has been lost or damaged, with when it happened, when it was reported, why, how it was reported, the estimated cost and whether it was settled, rejected or is still open. Closed claims carry the day they were closed.
Claims.grain: One row for each claim made on a policy
evidence: ClaimID unique, 850 rows, 900001-900850; PolicyID found in Policies (100%)
LossDate, ReportedDate and ClosedDate give three milestones; ClosedDate 4.82% missing, which equals Åben 41 of 850
ClaimStatus: Afsluttet (closed) 714, Afvist (rejected) 95, Åben (open) 41
ClaimCause 25 values, top Rudeskade 141, Vandskade 98; ReportedVia Selvbetjening på web 426, Telefon 290, App 134
EstimatedLossDKK 420-895,400
open_questions: Is ClosedDate also the decision date for rejected claims (Afvist)?
Claims.ai_notes: A policy has up to 3 claims (775 distinct policies in 850 claims). PolicyID + LossDate is unique. Danish values: Rudeskade = window damage, Vandskade = water damage, Selvbetjening på web = web self-service, Afvist = rejected, Åben = open.

beam.table_why: Three dates (LossDate, ReportedDate, ClosedDate) mark milestones of one claim, and ClosedDate is still empty for open claims.

ClaimID.why: The company's own identifier for each claim.

PolicyID.why: The policy the claim is made under; measured relationship, 100% found.

LossDate.why: The day the damage happened; present for every claim.

ReportedDate.why: The day the claim was reported; present for every claim.

ClosedDate.why: Empty exactly for the open claims.

ReportedVia.why: Says through which channel the claim arrived.

ClaimStatus.why: Decides whether ClosedDate applies; central to following claims through to settlement.

EstimatedLossDKK.why: The estimated cost of the loss; amounts can be summed over claims.

Coverages.description: The individual types of cover that can be part of a product, for example liability or fire, each marked as standard or optional, with the usual yearly price and deductible. A coverage belongs to one product.
Coverages.grain: One row for each type of cover offered under a product
evidence: CoverageID unique, 29 rows, 1-29; ProductID 1-6 found in Products (100%)
CoverageType: Standard 17, Tilvalg (optional) 12
BaseAnnualPremiumDKK 90-4,200 and DefaultDeductibleDKK 0-5,000; PolicyCoverages holds the actual DeductibleDKK and AnnualPremiumDKK per policy
CoverageName has 26 distinct values in 29 rows, e.g. Ansvar (3), Brand og eksplosion (2)
open_questions: The same CoverageName appears under several products (Ansvar 3 times): is each a separate cover with its own terms?
Coverages.ai_notes: CoverageName is not unique, so CoverageID, not the name, identifies a cover. Names are Danish (Ansvar = liability, Tyveri og indbrud = theft and burglary, Tilvalg = optional).

beam.table_why: One row per CoverageID with no dates or version columns.

CoverageID.why: The source's own identifier for each cover.

ProductID.why: Measured relationship: all 29 values are found in Products.ProductID.

BaseAnnualPremiumDKK.why: A list price for one cover; a price is not summed. The DKK unit is in the column name.

DefaultDeductibleDKK.why: The standard excess for the cover; the DKK unit is in the column name.

Customers.description: The private persons who have, or have had, insurance with the company, with their contact details, when they signed up and whether they are still customers. A customer who has cancelled stays in the list with a churn date.
Customers.grain: One row for each person who is a customer, whether still active or cancelled
evidence: CustomerID unique, 0% missing, 3,000 rows, integer 100001-103000
FirstName, LastName, BirthDate (1937-2007) and Gender (K 1,529, M 1,471) describe a person
CustomerStatus: Aktiv 2,541, Opsagt 459; ChurnDate filled for 15.3% of rows (84.7% missing), which matches the 459 Opsagt rows
Policies.CustomerID found in Customers.CustomerID for 5,640 of 5,640 values (100%)
open_questions: Is Email the customer's own address, given that up to 4 customers share one?
Is ChurnDate the day the customer asked to leave or the day the last policy ended?
Phone is unique where filled and 8% is missing: can a phone number be shared between customers?
Does MarketingConsent Ja/Nej record consent given at signup or the current choice?
Customers.ai_notes: Phone is also unique across all filled rows but is a contact detail, not the identity of the customer. Email has 2,629 distinct values in 2,918 filled rows, so some addresses are shared by several customers. AddressID is shared by up to 5 customers (2,773 distinct addresses in 3,000 rows). Contains personal data (names, birth dates, email, phone).

beam.table_why: One row per CustomerID and no validity dates or version columns, so only the current values are held. The user did not say how changes should be handled.

CustomerID.why: The company's own identifier for each customer; unique across all 3,000 rows.

FirstName.why: A customer is a named person, so the name should be filled in for every row.

LastName.why: A customer is a named person, so the name should be filled in for every row.

BirthDate.why: A person's date of birth does not change, and every customer should have one.

SignupDate.why: The day a customer joined does not change, and every customer has one.

Email.why: Shared by several customers in some cases (up to 4 rows with the same address) and missing for 2.73%; unclear whether it is the customer's own address.

AddressID.why: Measured relationship: all 3,000 values are found in Addresses.AddressID.

ChurnDate.why: Filled only for cancelled customers; unclear whether it is the day the customer asked to leave or the day the last policy ended.

Policies.description: An insurance agreement between a customer and the company for one product, with the day it started, the day it ended if it was cancelled, how often the customer pays and how it was sold. Cancelled policies stay in the table with their cancellation reason.
Policies.grain: One row for each insurance policy a customer takes out, identified by the policy number
evidence: PolicyID and PolicyNumber both unique, 5,640 rows, one-to-one
CustomerID found in Customers (100%), ProductID found in Products (100%)
PolicyStatus: Aktiv 4,595, Opsagt (cancelled) 1,045; EndDate and CancellationReason both 81.47% missing, so filled for 1,045 rows
StartDate 2008-01-06 to 2025-12-31; PaymentFrequency Månedlig 3,048, Årlig 1,439, Kvartalsvis 844, Halvårlig 309; SalesChannel Web 2,400, Telefon 1,200, Rådgiver 1,112, Partner 928
CustomerID + ProductID + StartDate unique; CustomerID + StartDate has 2 repeats
open_questions: InsuredAddressID is 53.81% missing: is it left empty for policies that insure no building (car, travel, accident), or is it missing data?
Policies.ai_notes: Customers hold up to 6 policies each (1,753 of 3,000 customers have more than one row). InsuredAddressID is filled for 2,605 rows. PolicyNumber has the form DK-year-number. PremiumInvoices.PolicyID covers 5,594 of 5,640 policies.

beam.table_why: One row per PolicyID. StartDate and EndDate are the life of the policy itself, not version dates of a repeated key, so the table keeps only the current state of each policy.

PolicyID.why: The source's own identifier for each policy; unique across 5,640 rows.

PolicyNumber.why: The number printed on the policy, in the form DK-year-number; unique and one-to-one with PolicyID.

CustomerID.why: Every policy belongs to a customer; measured relationship, 100% found.

ProductID.why: Every policy is for a product; measured relationship, 100% found.

InsuredAddressID.why: Measured relationship to Addresses; 53.81% missing without a clear reason.

StartDate.why: The day a policy starts is known for every row and does not change.

CancellationReason.why: Filled only when the policy is cancelled (Opsagt) and empty otherwise; same 81.47% missing as EndDate.

EndDate.why: Filled only for cancelled policies, same rows as CancellationReason.

PolicyCoverages.description: The covers that are included in each policy, with the sum insured, the deductible and the yearly premium agreed for that policy. It splits the price of a policy into its parts.
PolicyCoverages.grain: One row for each cover included in a policy, so a policy appears once for every cover it has
evidence: PolicyID + CoverageID unique together; no single column is unique; 20,787 rows
PolicyID found in Policies (100%), CoverageID found in Coverages (100%)
5,640 distinct policies and 29 distinct coverages
SumInsuredDKK 5.41% missing, 5,000-10,000,000; DeductibleDKK 0-7,500; AnnualPremiumDKK 68-6,752
open_questions: SumInsuredDKK is missing for 5.41% of rows: is it left empty for covers that have no insured sum, such as liability?
Does a policy's yearly premium equal the sum of AnnualPremiumDKK over its covers?
PolicyCoverages.ai_notes: A link between policies and coverages that also carries values of its own. SumInsuredDKK repeats the values 10,000,000 (1,617 rows) and 5,000,000 (522 rows), which look like fixed limits.

beam.table_why: A link between two things (policies and covers) rather than a thing or an event; its identity is the combination of the two keys, so the table type is left out.

PolicyID.why: Part of the identity of a row; 100% found in Policies.

CoverageID.why: Part of the identity of a row; 100% found in Coverages.

SumInsuredDKK.why: The amount insured for this cover on this policy; missing for 5.41% without explanation.

DeductibleDKK.why: The excess the customer pays on a claim; an amount that is not summed.

AnnualPremiumDKK.why: The yearly price of this cover on this policy; can be summed to a policy total.

PostalCodes.description: The list of Danish postal codes used in the data, each with its city and the region it belongs to. It places an address in a town and a region.
PostalCodes.grain: One row for each Danish postal area, identified by its four-digit code

Region has 5 values (Hovedstaden 18, Syddanmark 8, Midtjylland 8, Sjælland 5, Nordjylland 5), the five Danish regions

PostalCodes.ai_notes: City is also unique, but several Copenhagen postal codes carry a district suffix (København K, Ø, N, S, NV). Only 44 postal codes are present.

beam.table_why: One row per ZipCode, with no dates; a small reference list.

ZipCode.why: People use the four-digit postal code in the real world to identify a postal area.

City.why: Every postal code has a town name.

Region.why: Every postal code belongs to a region.

PremiumInvoices.description: A bill sent to a customer for the insurance premium of one policy for one period, with the invoice date, the due date, the period it covers, the amount and whether it has been paid, is overdue or is still open.

PremiumInvoices.ai_notes: The key measurements come from the first 50,000 rows only (sample). A policy has up to 36 invoices. Danish values: Betalt = paid, Forfalden = overdue, Åben = open.

beam.table_why: Several milestone dates (invoice, due, paid) for one invoice, with PaidDate empty until it is paid.

PolicyID.why: The policy that is billed; measured relationship, 100% found.

InvoiceDate.why: The day the invoice was issued.

PaidDate.why: Filled only when the invoice has been paid.

AmountDKK.why: The premium billed; can be summed over invoices and is central to revenue.

Products.ai_notes: ProductName is also unique and is how people refer to a product. Danish category values: Bolig = home, Bil = car, Dyr = pet.

beam.table_why: One row per ProductID with no dates or version columns.

ProductID.why: The source's own identifier for each product.

ProductName.why: People refer to a product by its name, and the name is unique across the 6 rows.
